## Scope

The credible-set helpers post-process marker posterior inclusion probabilities
(PIPs). They produce marginal-PIP-based sets; they are **not** automatically
equivalent to SuSiE-style per-effect credible sets and do not represent the
full posterior distribution over causal configurations.

## Regional PIPs and dense LD

`make_credible_sets_from_ld()` accepts a named PIP vector and a dense regional
LD/correlation matrix. Names are aligned when available. It repeatedly chooses
a lead by raw PIP or an LD-smoothed PIP score, keeps candidates with squared
correlation at least `min_r2`, orders them by PIP, and accumulates them until
`coverage` is reached.

`pip_cutoff` zeroes very small PIPs before construction. `allow_incomplete`
controls whether an under-coverage candidate set is returned. `remove` chooses
whether later leads exclude the complete lead LD neighborhood or only markers
already placed in the credible set. Multiple sets can be returned.

## Credible sets from fitted models

`make_credible_sets()` reads PIPs from `fit$dm` in current STBLR fit objects.
Select a trait by name or one-based column index. Supply either:

- predefined marker `sets` plus dense regional `LD`; or
- a `Glist` containing `Glist$sparseLD$prefix`, allowing regional dense LD to
  be extracted from the stored CSR.

When `sets = NULL`, the helper defines loci from marker positions using
`locus_pip_cutoff`, `max_locus_distance`, and `max_loci`. It returns `summary`,
nested `sets`, complete `locus_sets`, `loci`, resolved `parameters`, and the
selected `trait`.

Sparse LD must have been constructed with a window and `r2_threshold`
permissive enough for the requested `min_r2`. Missing edges are treated as
zero and cannot be recovered during post-processing.

```r
cs <- make_credible_sets(
  fit,
  Glist = Glist,
  trait = 1,
  coverage = 0.95,
  min_r2 = 0.5,
  pip_cutoff = 0.001
)
```

## Multiple signals

`make_multisignal_credible_sets_from_ld()` is an approximate marginal-PIP
procedure. `min_signal_pip`, `signal_coverage`, `max_signals`, and the marker
removal rule determine whether additional LD-separated sets are attempted.
Interpret the result as a post-processing summary, not a fitted per-effect
model.

## Global extraction and local refitting

A recommended default is to fit the genome-wide summary model once and then
extract loci:

- `extract_stblr_finemap_loci()` summarizes `fit$dm` and `fit$bm` within
  supplied loci and optionally constructs single- or multi-signal sets. It does
  not rerun MCMC.
- `finemap_stblr_csr()` performs explicit local CSR sensitivity/reference
  refits. It fixes global `ve`, `vb`, and inclusion probability estimates,
  optionally residualizes regional summary scores against effects outside the
  locus, and aggregates independent local runs.

Local refitting is not a replacement for the global fit and may answer a
different conditional question. Report both the global selection mechanism
and local controls, including any optional LD-swap proposal settings.

## Alignment and interpretation

Marker IDs in PIPs, LD, `Glist`, locus sets, and map data must refer to the same
allele orientation and order. Dense LD is intended for regional use;
`Glist$sparseLD` supports scalable regional extraction. A high credible-set
coverage value is a cumulative marginal-PIP target, not a calibrated guarantee
that exactly one causal variant lies in the returned set.

See [`?make_credible_sets`](https://github.com/psoerensen/sblr/blob/master/man/make_credible_sets.Rd),
[`?make_credible_sets_from_ld`](https://github.com/psoerensen/sblr/blob/master/man/make_credible_sets_from_ld.Rd),
and the [sparse-LD workflow](sparse_ld_workflows.qmd).
